gen-dafont-verve-fs-paquito: Confident in its own way, Verve packs heavy verticals tight against hairline strokes. Paquito, a classic serif, does its best work low and sturdy, with caps sitting barely above the lowercase.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-supreme: Approachable but sharp-edged, Verve pairs dark thick stems with feathery joins and bowls that nearly close. And Supreme keeps its letters open and crisp, a heavy-looking sans strip of text that never curls shut.
gen-dafont-verve-manrope: Manrope draws every curve with a bright open mouth and one steady line width, nothing like the closed shapes above it. Verve's heavy stems and threadlike joins make a sharp contrast.
gen-dafont-verve-satoshi: Sharp bright edges set against fat darkness give Verve its look, with bowls nearly sealed shut. Satoshi's soaring x-height and open e supply the opposite: rods instead of blades.
gen-dafont-verve-work-sans: Work Sans draws its letters with marker-like plainness. Verve's weighty stems and razor-thin arcs sit against open c tips and a high mean line, and that clash of closed and open is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-walkway-fs-gambetta: Graceful and bookish, Gambetta, a text serif, carries wide channels into each counter and crossbars a touch thinner than its stems. Walkway sits low and compact up top, so its hooked c is the job it does best.
gen-dafont-walkway-fs-karma: A broad open hook of a c gives Walkway its signature, packed into a compact string of letters. And Karma, a text serif, stands taller in the lowercase with calm modulation, so it may deserve a slightly smaller size.
gen-dafont-walkway-fs-recia: Sharp and authoritative, Recia is a text serif whose thick-and-thin rhythm shows mainly on close inspection. Recia's generous openings hold at every weight, which is a good reason to give it a bit more size than Walkway's low, tight letters.
gen-dafont-walkway-lora: Walkway tucks a broad hooked c into a compact line of letters with no slack in them. But Lora, a classic serif, thins mildly like soft metal stamping, so its size can stay modest and still read clearly.
gen-dafont-zag-fs-literata: Tight tracking and oversized small letters define Zag. Literata, the serif below, stays sturdy, with stems only a shade heavier than its arms, while Zag earns its keep big and short.
